notes: §1985:XIV.3.5.4 GR2: for an input-output CD "the content of the data item specified by data-name-3 (SYMBOLIC TERMINAL) ... designates the source of the message". For CommunicationFormat.InputOutput Receive reads the name at positions 15-26 (CommunicationArea.SourceName), answers 21 (Table 1, symbolic source unknown) for a terminal the MCS does not define, and otherwise takes the next message from that terminal (TakeFromTerminal); LockedTerminalChanged makes a changed SYMBOLIC TERMINAL after the first statement unsuccessful with 21 (§1985:XIV.2.2.4 GR31). The witness is an unknown terminal with NO DATA. Probes at --std 85 (classes b, d): TERM1 returned T1-FIR key 0 then ST key 2 (remainder), a two-segment message ABCD key 2 under MESSAGE, T1-THI key 0 and RD key 2 under SEGMENT; changing CD-TERM to TERM2 afterwards gave 21 with the receiver untouched; NOTERM as the first name gave 21 and locked the CD, as GR31 requires.

next.reason: 1985: "If cd-name-1 references an input-output CD, the content of the data item specified by data-name-3 (SYMBOLIC TERMINAL) ... designates the source"; 2023: "The 2023 RECEIVE has no cd-name or CD: "data-name-1 is an implementor-defined value that identifies the run unit that sent a message"". 2023 has no communication description entries or SYMBOLIC TERMINAL. Its RECEIVE takes messages between run units by message tag, so the CD-based source rule is gone.
